clue.text: Tuba player perhaps lets tinnitus mar playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being performed in a fresh arrangement rather than as written

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A brass player worries that ringing in the ears will ruin the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba player is one example of a musician who plays an instrument, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dust busting is extremely important

blocks.note: dust and earth are both loose soil
busting means breaking apart

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a dust explosion is a very big deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is momentous, of huge significance, which is what extremely important means.

clue.text: Flamboyant Versace tie might be brought out in the afternoon?

definitions.text: might be brought out in the afternoon?

indicators.note: flamboyant means showy and extravagant, so the letters are flung into a showier new order

blocks.note: the designer's name plus a necktie supply the letters

explanation.surface: A showy designer necktie gets an outing at a smart afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: a fancy set of cups and saucers is what comes out at afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of teapot, cups and saucers is laid out for the British custom of afternoon tea.

clue.text: Stop talking and start to surmount inhibitions

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to end a phone call by putting the receiver down
the opening letter of surmount

explanation.surface: Advice to stay quiet and begin overcoming your shyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang-ups are emotional problems or neuroses that hold a person back, much like inhibitions.

clue.text: Man possibly upset Elsie baselessly

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom letter, and losing the base removes the final letter
upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the remaining letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the woman's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A man perhaps unsettled a woman called Elsie without any grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, the self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: The exact thing!

blocks.note: first meaning: the English word 'the' is the grammatical example of this
second meaning: an idiom for the genuine, real thing itself

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a cry of 'that's exactly it!'; but the word 'The' is itself the example, and the idiom gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call 'the' this kind of determiner, and colloquially the phrase also means the genuine or authentic item.

clue.text: Average man inter alia could be an MP

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else if rearranged

blocks.note: par is the normal or average level
these letters are the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ordinary man, among other things, might become a Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Inter alia is Latin for 'among other things'; MP stands for Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is a member of a legislative assembly, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: American is treated privately

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so its letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient from the US receives medical care in confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase describes proceedings held in a judge's chambers, away from the public, so in private.

clue.text: Watch tool going up and down

definitions.note: the answer is a noun or verb; the definition describes its motion

blocks.note: to watch is to see
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the implement as it moves up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece, but it is the verb meaning look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank pivoted in the middle rises and falls, and to move in that alternating way is to do this.

clue.text: Statistics about university's standing

indicators.note: about means around, so one item goes round the other

blocks.note: the informal short form of statistics
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Numbers about an institution's ranking in the league tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Status and standing both mean one's position or rank relative to others.

clue.text: Intriguer ill-advisedly giving refuge to fighter

indicators.note: giving refuge means sheltering, so the words shelter the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the next

explanation.surface: A schemer unwisely shelters an insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-advisedly' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in order inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla is an irregular soldier in a small independent band, so a type of fighter.

clue.text: Filth turning children's stomachs

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: smut is dirt or obscene material

explanation.surface: Disgusting material makes young people feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning children's stomachs' reads as an idiom for nausea; 'turning' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tum is the childish or informal word for stomach, so the plural is a nursery-talk form of stomachs.

clue.text: Mitt Romney perhaps making poor calibre pun

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are in a bad order and need rearranging

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US politician cracks a feeble joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitt Romney was the Republican Party's 2012 US presidential candidate, so he is an example of a party member.

clue.text: Some burning feminists didn't want their support

definitions.text: Some burning feminists didn't want their support

blocks.clueFragment: Some burning feminists didn't want their support
blocks.note: surface reading: some activists withdrew their backing from a cause
setter's reading: the famous image of feminists burning their underwear, so the support is a garment

explanation.surface: Some passionate campaigners refused to give their backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning' seems to mean fervent, and 'support' seems to mean backing; both point instead to the legendary 1960s bra-burning protests.
explanation.definitionFit: These undergarments support the bust, and they were famously said to be burned by protesting feminists.

clue.text: "Potty" Anglicans with sheepish fellow in charge

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a ram is a male sheep
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Crazy churchgoers are put under the command of a shy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like 'mad', but the quotation marks hint at a pottery sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots are made of fired clay, so something pot-like is earthenware, a fired-clay material.

clue.text: One bets with silver and sovereigns

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ER is the monarch's royal cipher; two monarchs give it twice

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes silver and gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' looks like gold coins but means two monarchs, each ER (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: A wagerer is a person who places a stake on an outcome, i.e. someone who bets.

clue.text: The socialists of France gave up

blocks.note: the political left is the socialist wing
taken as written
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: The French socialist party quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off is to stop doing something, which is to cease or abandon it.

clue.text: Initially shy and timid, they say they have a speech impediment

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the opening letters of shy and timid
people who say things are utterers

explanation.surface: Bashful, nervous people find it hard to talk fluently.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'they have a speech impediment', with 'they' as the link; the answer is people with a stammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stutterers are people who repeat sounds involuntarily when talking, a common kind of speech disorder.

clue.text: Liturgy correctly pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: correctly means right; spoken, it matches a ceremonial word

explanation.surface: Church services spoken with proper diction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like part of the surface about saying words properly but signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a prescribed religious ceremony, and a liturgy is a fixed form of public worship.

clue.text: There's none left, OK?

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: every one is on the right side, with none on the left
second meaning: satisfactory, fine

explanation.walkthrough: 'none left' sounds like an empty plate, but it is a whimsical reading: if nothing is left, everything is right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday expression for acceptable or satisfactory, and literally says every item is on the right.

clue.text: Gloomy looking youth bought drug

blocks.note: got means obtained or bought
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A miserable-faced teenager purchased narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A goth is a member of a subculture who wears black clothes and pale makeup, a dark, gloomy appearance.

clue.text: He's left his country, appallingly grim part of Eastern Europe

indicators.note: appallingly means dreadfully, so the letters are in a dreadful state and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: An exile describes the bleak corner of Eastern Europe he fled.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has emigrated from their homeland, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Enjoy ultimate internet service

blocks.note: to enjoy a right is to have the use of it
net means final, as in net result

explanation.surface: Make the most of the best online provider.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is an early worldwide internet discussion system of newsgroups, a service running over the network.

clue.text: Casual lot eat at others' expense

blocks.note: free means relaxed and informal
a load is a lot, as in loads of money

explanation.surface: A relaxed group dines while someone else pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot eat' tempts an anagram, but the pieces are simple synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeload is to take food or hospitality from others without paying or contributing.
